summary: All 16 units reviewed in full. Every numeric key and worked example was recomputed independently in Python (kinematics, projectile motion, the Euler golf-ball range table 132.1/126.5/123.6/122.1 m, the 120.6 m extrapolated range which a fixed-step RK4 run also reproduces at 120.58 m, relative motion, Earth and Mars orbital constants, energy, momentum, impact, polar and path coordinates, drag) and all match the stated keys, tolerances, signs, units and g = 9.81; every MCQ has exactly one correct option matching the key. The relative-motion 'minimum drift' marking point is physically correct. No literal unicode-escape text, '[object Object]' or garbled non-Latin characters were found. Only minor wording and consistency problems remain. This was an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: Lesson text says 'the cross-stream component of v_b must be zero in the along-stream direction'. This is garbled: it is the along-stream (downstream) component of the ground velocity that must be zero.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to: 'to reach the point directly opposite, the along-stream component of the ground velocity must be zero, so the boat must aim upstream'.

issues.problem: The marking point 'aim upstream so the downstream drift angle is as small as possible, which occurs when the boat's velocity relative to the water is perpendicular to the resulting ground track' is correct (for v_w > v_b the minimum-drift track satisfies sin(alpha) = v_b/v_w, alpha measured from the line straight across). However 'drift angle' is not defined and this strategy is not taught in the lesson or worked examples, so a student cannot be expected to produce it.
issues.suggestedFix: Define the drift angle (angle of the ground track from the perpendicular to the banks), give the heading cos(theta) = v_b/v_w measured from the upstream direction, add one sentence to the lesson, or mark the point as an extension not required for full marks.

issues.problem: Stem says 'A vehicle travels around a frictionless banked curve at a speed above the design speed' and then asks what the friction force must do. A frictionless road has no friction force, so the stem contradicts the question.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword: 'A vehicle rounds a banked curve designed for frictionless cornering at a speed above the design speed. To avoid sliding up the bank, the friction force from the road must...'. The key (act down the slope) is correct.

issues.problem: Hook says the ISS 'never needs an engine to keep up that speed'. The ISS loses altitude to residual atmospheric drag and is periodically reboosted; the claim holds only in the lesson's drag-free idealisation.
issues.suggestedFix: Say it needs no thrust to maintain its orbit in the drag-free idealisation (in practice small periodic reboosts offset residual drag). The 92 min and 7.7 km/s figures are acceptable.

issues.problem: Lesson sentence 'Because the force has no transverse component, only the radial speed changes it; the transverse velocity adjusts so that m r v_theta stays constant' is confusing: a central force changes the radial velocity but is not itself changed by it.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword: 'Because the force has no transverse component it cannot change m r v_theta; as r changes the transverse speed adjusts so that m r v_theta stays constant'.

issues.problem: Lesson states a planar force is conservative 'if and only if' the mixed partial derivatives agree, without the simply-connected-region condition (mentioned only in the q009 marking guide).
issues.suggestedFix: Add 'on a simply connected region' to the lesson statement so it matches the marking guide.
